newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Ortiz says certification may affect mkts.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Ortiz says certification may affect mkts.

text.p: Mexican Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz said Thursday that the so-called certification process, in which the U.S. government certifies whether Mexico is an ally in the fight against drug trafficking, could affect Mexican financial markets.
But Ortiz also said the impact would not be strong.

U.S. law requires the certification of those countries due to receive financial aid to combat international drug trafficking. Mexican commentators regularly assail the certification process as U.S. meddling in Mexican affairs.

"Of course it will affect the cooperation in the fight against drug trafficking, and this is not good for the economy and nor is it good for the markets," Ortiz told journalists after attending a meeting of government, business and labor leaders.

"I don't believe the effects will be very strong in the short term if the certification is not given, but certainly the environment of coooperation favors economic activity and the markets," he added.
